newsitem.title: USA: News Corp not planning HarperCollins sale.
newsitem.headline: News Corp not planning HarperCollins sale.

text.p: News Corp said Monday it has no plans to sell its HarperCollins book publishing unit.
In a statement, the company said it is "reaffirming its long-term commitment to the business."

It acknowledged it sometimes receives "expressions of interest" about its businesses, including HarperCollins, and was issuing a statement "as a result of unusual speculation in the media about the future of HarperCollins."
News said its 1997 year results would include an extraordinary charge of US$270 million related to a restructuring of the book publisher.
The charge comes after the company completed a year-long restructuring at the book publisher.
The company said the restructuring and review "improves its profitability" and allows the division to "publish more dynamically in a competitive marketplace."
The publisher said it "will focus its publishing efforts on a defined number of strategic areas..."
A spokesman said the unit will scale back in non-commercial fiction.

In the statement, News Chairman Rupert Murdoch said: HarperCollins is a key asset and immensely important to our company...(and) plays an important role in each of the primary geographic areas where the company conducts considerable business."
